judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer does not challenge the characterization of Sun_2022's simulation as generic 'simulation' vs. 'electromagnetic (EM) field simulation'. The reviewer's check item 1 in the math audit actually validates Eq. 5 (the calibrated visibility) as correct, and no flag is raised about the methodological description of Sun_2022's contribution being too generic or mischaracterizing the cited paper's method.

The review mentions electromagnetic simulations in its own summary, but it does not specifically challenge the paper's citation to Sun_2022 or claim that the cited source is mischaracterised as generic 'simulation' rather than EM-field simulation. Under the broadened-claim rule, no source-specific contradiction is flagged.
The reviewer does not mention the paper Sun_2022 or the description of its simulation methodology anywhere in the report.

The reviewer's numerical results audit section appears truncated and contains no mention of the 570 MHz vs 750 MHz inconsistency. The reviewer does reference '750 MHz' in the context of discussing the fringe phase for the 3.2m baselines, but never flags the internal inconsistency between '570 MHz' in Sec. 3.3 and '750 MHz' elsewhere.

The reviewer repeatedly refers to 750 MHz, but does not identify any inconsistency involving 570 MHz or flag the same-paper mismatch between Sec. 3.3 and other locations. There is no explicit numerical error report corresponding to the digit swap.
While the reviewer critiques aspects of Section 3.3, they fail to identify the 570 MHz value or the inconsistency with the 750 MHz value used elsewhere.

The reviewer explicitly PASSES Eq. 5 in the mathematical consistency audit, noting 'The geometrical mapping of the fringe phase e^{-2pi i / lambda (r_j - r_i) · n} is standard and correct for a general interferometric baseline.' The reviewer did not detect that the equation actually contains pi i / lambda (missing the factor of 2) — in fact the reviewer reproduced the correct formula as if it were what appears in the paper.

The reviewer explicitly says Eq. (5) is correct: "The geometrical mapping of the fringe phase e^{-\frac{2\pi i}{\lambda} (\vec{r}_j - \vec{r}_i) \cdot \vec{n}} is standard and correct" and instead flags Eq. (10) for omitting the phase term entirely. This does not detect the injected halving of the coefficient in Eq. (5).
The reviewer explicitly audits Eq. (5) in the mathematical consistency section and marks it as correct, quoting the canonical 2pi coefficient and thus failing to notice the injected pi coefficient.

The reviewer does not flag the contradiction between the Methods claim of jointly combining all 12 baselines in a stacked likelihood versus the Results section using only 3 baselines (A1-A9, A2-A10, A4-A12). No mention of this inconsistency appears anywhere in the review.

The review criticizes missing likelihood and MCMC details in Sec. 2.4/3.3, but never flags the specific contradiction that Methods claims all 12 baselines are jointly combined while Results uses only 3 baselines. No specific cross-section protocol inconsistency matching this injection is identified.
The reviewer identifies issues with the likelihood and MCMC details in the relevant sections but does not flag the contradiction regarding the number of baselines (12 vs 3).
